newsitem.title: JAPAN: North Korea's Kim attends military parade.
newsitem.headline: North Korea's Kim attends military parade.

text.p: North Korea's de facto leader Kim Jong-il attended a military parade on Friday to celebrate his late president's 85th birthday as well as the 65th anniversary of the army, official media reported.
Soldiers marched before Kim while waving the banner of the late president Kim Il-sung and the army flag, the official Korea Central News Agency (KCNA) said in a report monitored in Tokyo.
"When supreme commander of the KPA (Korean People's Army) comrade Kim Jong-il appeared on the platform a storm of cheers burst forth," KCNA said.

Kim Jong-il, supreme commander of the country's 1.1 million-strong military, has yet to be formally confirmed in two key posts held by his late father Kim Il-sung -- general secretary of the ruling Workers' Party and state president.
Korea watchers believe Kim Jong-il, who rarely makes public appearances, is likely to formally assume the posts after the third anniversary of his father's death in July.
